name: CA-32
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district with a +14 partisan lean
Sherman is a well-funded incumbent with $2.7M on hand
Thompson has raised only ~$34K with negligible cash
Prediction markets price Sherman near certain to win
model.rationale: Brad Sherman holds a heavily Democratic seat and outpaces Larry Thompson by an enormous fundraising margin, while markets price the race as effectively decided. With no competitive polling or expert ratings suggesting otherwise, the fundamentals point to a comfortable Sherman win.
model.watch: A surprise surge of outside spending against Sherman or an unusually favorable Republican national environment could narrow the margin, though not plausibly enough to threaten the seat.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Brad Sherman, a long-serving Democratic incumbent, is seeking another term in this Los Angeles-area district that leans Democratic by about fourteen points. He advanced to the general election and enters with roughly $2.7 million in cash on hand after raising over $2.5 million, supplemented by outside support.

His Republican opponent, Larry Thompson, has raised only about $34,000 and reports minimal cash remaining, with no meaningful outside spending on either side. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets give Sherman roughly a 95 percent chance of winning. The combination of district lean, incumbency, and the financial imbalance makes this a safe Democratic seat.
